name: Bupropion
addictionPotential: moderate addictive potential; higher with insufflation; can produce dependence at both therapeutic and recreational doses
toxicities: Seizure risk increases with dose. LD50 in rats and mice is moderate. Overdose may cause monoamine storm, seizures, cardiac arrest, or stroke.
summary: Bupropion is a cathinone-class NDRI (norepinephrine-dopamine reuptake inhibitor) and nicotinic acetylcholine receptor antagonist. It is used clinically for major depressive disorder, smoking cessation, and off-label for ADHD and SAD. It has both stimulant and deliriant-like effects at high doses.
effectsSummary: Stimulation, increased heart rate and blood pressure, appetite suppression, nausea, pupil dilation, motivation enhancement, dream potentiation, anxiety, potential for seizures at high doses. At very high doses: delirium, hallucinations, paranoia.
dosageRemark: Seizure risk is dose-dependent. Maximum recommended daily dose is 450mg. Immediate release, sustained release, and controlled release formulations have different dosing schedules.
generalRisks: Seizures, increased heart rate and blood pressure, anxiety, insomnia, nausea, dry mouth. Higher risk of seizures at doses above 450mg/day. Can cause mania in bipolar patients.
longtermRisks: Seizure risk, especially at high doses. Weight loss. May increase anxiety. Can cause dependence. Deliriant effects at very high doses.
saferUse: Do not crush or chew extended-release tablets
Monitor for mood changes and suicidal thoughts
